clue.text: Intolerable and badly done-by, help mate with no source of money

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters gathered here are knocked out of shape and reordered
with no tells us to drop a letter from the word mate
the source of a word is its opening letter, here the start of money

explanation.surface: Someone hard done by, helping a friend while broke, finds the situation unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no source of money' removes M from MATE, leaving ATE; 'badly' then rearranges DONEBY + HELP + ATE into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: behaviour outside the bounds of acceptability is beyond the pale, i.e. unacceptable or intolerable.

clue.text: Spreads, say, in case of bugs

indicators.note: in places the word for say within the outer shell of bugs
the case of a word is its outside letters, here the first and last of bugs

parts.note: to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where to put spreads, perhaps inside a box of insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of bugs' gives B and S, which hold UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine and similar dairy products are spreads for bread, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Standard staff needed to support police HQ

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so the staff goes below the police HQ

parts.note: Scotland Yard, the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, is often just the Yard
a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A standard-issue staff is required to prop up police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed to support' places STICK below YARD in this down entry; Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure or criterion against which things are judged is a standard, a synonym.

clue.text: Ignorant of rising water in France

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evian is a French brand of mineral water from Évian-les-Bains

explanation.surface: Someone unaware of the rising water level in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EVIAN upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking experience or knowledge, innocent and ignorant of the world, is a close synonym.

clue.text: Multi-layered, the answer's right up a touch

indicators.note: in a down entry moving up a touch means shifting a letter one place higher

parts.note: an answer is a reply; the 's is absorbed into the surface

explanation.surface: Something layered is described, with the answer apparently pushed slightly upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + REPLY gives THEREPLY; 'up a touch' shifts R one place higher in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool or plywood made of three strands or layers is described with this term, so it is multi-layered.

clue.text: Birds, for example, rest in flight

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, meaning for example

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Birds, for instance, take a break while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flight' rearranges REST into RETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons with white plumage are wading birds, so the plural fits this clue.

clue.text: Granting unusually draconic start to government

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of draconic are arranged in an unexpected way
the start to a word is its first letter, here of government

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly harsh beginning to an administration is being allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granting' reads like 'admittedly' opening a sentence, but it is the participle meaning conceding; 'unusually' yields ACCORDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord someone something is to give or concede it, so the participle matches granting.

clue.text: Surplus may be invested in index tracker

indicators.note: money invested in a fund sits inside it, so the letters lie within index tracker

explanation.surface: Excess cash might be put into an index-tracking fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional beyond what is needed is spare or surplus, a synonym.

clue.text: This may be taken as commitment

definitions.text: This may be taken as commitment

parts.words: This may be taken as commitment
parts.note: the idiom 'take the ___' means to commit oneself to a bold course of action

explanation.surface: Something that might be accepted as a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'take the plunge' means deciding firmly to do something risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive or leap into something is what one takes when finally committing to a decision.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in a tier of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a wandering dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line, TIER, which goes 'about' ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of dog, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Reading music

definitions.meaning: a recitation or public reading of a text
a musical performance by a soloist or small group

explanation.surface: Reading music, as a pianist at practice does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' tempts as the Berkshire town; here it is a public delivery of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a spoken rendition of a text and a solo concert performance.

clue.text: Follow gent inside to institute legal proceedings

indicators.note: the inside of gent is its middle letters

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A man inside is followed up with a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gent inside' gives EN, the middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a consequence, so it means follow.

clue.text: Create a diversion in harbour

definitions.meaning: to amuse or keep people diverted
to hold an idea or feeling in mind, as in considering it

explanation.surface: Causing a distraction in a port, as in a military raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' looks like a port, but here it is the verb: to harbour a hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to amuse guests and to hold a thought in mind, as with entertaining doubts.

clue.text: Son's design of replica vent for breathing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

indicators.note: a design of something rearranges its parts into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A son makes a model air vent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' rearranges REPLICA into PIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects and whales breathe through such an opening, a respiratory vent in anatomy.

clue.text: Intended recipient of speech on European energy

indicators.note: in a down entry on means the earlier piece sits on top of the later ones

parts.note: an address is a formal speech
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Who a speech about European energy is aimed at.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter or message is sent to is its recipient, the meaning of the term.

clue.text: Face struggle, accepting decline

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
to sag is to sink or decline

explanation.surface: Confront the fight while conceding a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb here, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for the face or a person's features is visage.

clue.text: Strikingly attractive actor must be gutted not working

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of actor

parts.note: resting is the theatrical euphemism for an actor without work

explanation.surface: An unemployed actor ends up devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves AR from ACTOR; 'resting' is stage slang for an actor out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eye-catching that stops you in your tracks is arresting, so striking.

clue.text: Tribal chief's love child, say, turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading the letters from the bottom

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a minor is a child in law
EG, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A tribal leader's love child appears unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses OMINOREG in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Apache leader is a well-known example of a tribal chief.

clue.text: Help to accommodate most of relations with love for martial art

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: most of a word loses its final letter

parts.note: kin are one's relations
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Assistance housing family members alongside affection becomes a fighting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with love for' looks like a substitution, but 'for' is only a link: O simply ends the answer; 'most of' drops the last letter of the relations word.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese self-defence discipline is one example of a martial art.

clue.text: Article on churchman from a range

indicators.note: in a down entry on places the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: An article about a clergyman who comes from a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from the Andes mountain range in South America.

clue.text: Natural boundary providing advantage in hotel dispute

indicators.note: in places the word for advantage within the other pieces

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a row is a dispute or quarrel
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Gaining the upper hand during an argument at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs and trees marking a field edge is a living, natural boundary.

clue.text: Dries up, accompanied by the Queen on last of duties

indicators.note: in a down entry on places the earlier pieces above the final one

parts.note: with means accompanied by
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of duties

explanation.surface: Someone flagging while accompanying the monarch on her final engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that withers shrivels as it loses moisture, so it dries up.

clue.text: Elgar denies being outside such a fertile region

indicators.note: the words Elgar denies sit outside the answer, which lies concealed within them

explanation.surface: The composer Elgar refuses to be outdoors in such a lush area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being outside' signals that the words around the answer enclose it; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is cultivated, fertile ground, and a fertile region can be called the garden of a country.

clue.text: Rail about reformed peers and criminal

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a dado rail runs along a wall at waist height

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining about reformed aristocrats and a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a verb (rant) but is DADO; 'reformed' rearranges PEERS into ESPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw, especially in the Wild West, is a desperado, so a criminal.

clue.text: Dross incorporating new words commonly used

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece into the body of a word

parts.note: slag is dross, the waste from smelting

explanation.surface: Rubbish that includes new everyday vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal vocabulary used in everyday speech rather than formal writing is slang.

clue.text: European caught in worst attack

indicators.note: caught in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them, as is to best them

explanation.surface: A European is caught up in the worst assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' looks like a superlative but is the verb meaning defeat, BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to assail or trouble from all sides, so it means attack.

clue.text: International covered by deep- toned foundation

indicators.note: covered by means placed inside another piece

parts.note: bass describes a deep-toned voice or sound

explanation.surface: A worldwide ground layer hidden under something with a deep sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying support on which something rests is its base or foundation.

clue.text: Collected a service note by front door

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last letter follows on

parts.note: Mass is a church service
E is a musical note

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here of door

explanation.surface: Collected a church-service musical note by the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate, so the past form means collected.

clue.text: Energise one part of church after end of sermon

indicators.note: after puts the church part following the end of sermon

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of sermon

parts.note: a spire is the tall tower top of a church

explanation.surface: A preacher wakes up one part of the church after the sermon ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to fill them with enthusiasm, which is to energise them.

clue.text: Talk by nursery producing methane, for example

parts.note: a greenhouse is a nursery for young plants
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: Chatter in a plant nursery producing methane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk' and 'by' read as chat nearby, but GAS simply sits beside the nursery word.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane traps heat in the atmosphere, so it is one example of a planet-warming gas.
